questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (3F)$ for the vector field $F$ where

$$
F=(2yx+{x}^{2})\,i+(5-{y}^{3})\,j-2yz\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (3F)=3∇\cdot F.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2yx+{x}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(5-{y}^{3})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(-2yz) \\  & =2y+2x-3{y}^{2}-2y \\  & =2x-3{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (3F) & =3∇\cdot F \\  & =3(2x-3{y}^{2}) \\  & =6x-9{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (F+G)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F=y\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,i-{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,j,\,∇\cdot G=2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)) \\  & =-2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)-2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) \\  & =-4y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (F+G) & =∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G \\  & =-4y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) \\  & =-2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (2F+G)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F={e}^{5x}\,i+y{e}^{3y}\,j,\,∇\cdot G=3{e}^{5x}-2{e}^{3y}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (2F+G) & =∇\cdot (2F)+∇\cdot G \\  & =2∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{5x})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{3y}) \\  & =5{e}^{5x}+{e}^{3y}+3y{e}^{3y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (2F+G) & =2∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G \\  & =2\cdot (5{e}^{5x}+{e}^{3y}+3y{e}^{3y})+3{e}^{5x}-2{e}^{3y} \\  & =10{e}^{5x}+2{e}^{3y}+6y{e}^{3y}+3{e}^{5x}-2{e}^{3y} \\  & =13{e}^{5x}+6y{e}^{3y}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (F-2G)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F={x}^{2}y\,i+{y}^{2}\,j,\,∇\cdot G=xy+{y}^{2}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (F-2G) & =∇\cdot F-∇\cdot (2G) \\  & =∇\cdot F-2∇\cdot G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y)+\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =2xy+2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (F-2G) & =∇\cdot F-2∇\cdot G \\  & =2xy+2y-2\cdot (xy+{y}^{2}) \\  & =2xy+2y-2xy-2{y}^{2} \\  & =2y-2{y}^{2} \\  & =2y(1-y).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F)$ for the vector field $F$ where

$$
F=x{e}^{2x}\,i-y{e}^{2x}\,j+x{z}^{2}\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F)=\frac{1}{2}∇\cdot F.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{2x})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-y{e}^{2x})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x{z}^{2}) \\  & ={e}^{2x}+2x{e}^{2x}-{e}^{2x}+2xz \\  & =2x{e}^{2x}+2xz.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F) & =\frac{1}{2}∇\cdot F \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (2x{e}^{2x}+2xz) \\  & =x{e}^{2x}+xz.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We will use the following identity:

$$
∇\cdot (f\,F)=f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f
$$

First, we compute $∇\cdot F$ and $∇f.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =⟨y,x,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡z⟩, \\ ∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{4}{y}{sin}^{2}⁡z)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{z}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{sin}⁡z)=\operatorname{cos}⁡z.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (f\,F) & =f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f \\  & =(xy+2\operatorname{cos}⁡z)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡z+⟨\frac{4}{y}{sin}^{2}⁡z,x{z}^{2},\operatorname{sin}⁡z⟩\cdot ⟨y,x,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡z⟩ \\  & =xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z+2{cos}^{2}⁡z+4{sin}^{2}⁡z+{x}^{2}{z}^{2}-2{sin}^{2}⁡z \\  & =xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z+{x}^{2}{z}^{2}+2({sin}^{2}⁡z+{cos}^{2}⁡z) \\  & =xy\operatorname{cos}⁡z+{x}^{2}{z}^{2}+2.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Calculate $\nabla \cdot (\mathbf{F}-3\mathbf{G})$ for the vector fields $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G,$ where

$$
\mathbf{F}=\left(x^2+y\right)\,\mathbf{i}+ \left(xy-y^2\right)\,\mathbf{j}, \quad \nabla \cdot \mathbf{G}=x+y.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $\nabla \cdot (k \mathbf F) = k \nabla \cdot \mathbf F$

- $\nabla \cdot (\mathbf F + \mathbf G) = \nabla \cdot \mathbf F + \nabla \cdot \mathbf G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (F-3G) & =∇\cdot (F)+∇\cdot (-3G) \\  & =∇\cdot F-3∇\cdot G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $\nabla \cdot \mathbf{F}.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+y)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy-{y}^{2}) \\  & =2x+x-2y \\  & =3x-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (F-3G) & =∇\cdot F-3∇\cdot G \\  & =(3x-2y)-3\cdot (x+y) \\  & =-5y.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Given that $\mathbf F(x,y) = \left\langle \dfrac 1x, xy \right \rangle$ and $f(x,y) = \dfrac 1{x},$ calculate $\nabla \cdot (f\,\mathbf F).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We will use the following identity:

$$
\nabla \cdot (f\,\mathbf F) = f\, \nabla \cdot \mathbf {F}+  \mathbf F \cdot \nabla f
$$

First, we compute $\nabla \cdot \mathbf {F}$ and $\nabla f.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =⟨-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}},0⟩, \\ ∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{x})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)=-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}+x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (f\,F) & =f\,∇\cdot F+F\cdot ∇f \\  & =\frac{1}{x}(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}+x)+⟨\frac{1}{x},xy⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}},0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}+1-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}} \\  & =1-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$
